title: DMC3 HD class layout read out of constructor stores

records.title: A store of a vtable into the first argument identifies a constructor
records.summary: A constructor writes its class's vtable into the object at offset zero. Following the register the Microsoft x64 convention puts the first argument in, and the register a RIP-relative lea filled, finds 270 such stores of a taken address into that object. 265 of them store a known vtable, which at ninety-eight per cent is a check on the following rather than a result of it: an address written into an object at a fixed offset, taken by lea in a function whose first argument that object is, is overwhelmingly a vtable. 146 functions store one at offset zero and are therefore constructors or destructors of that vtable's class, named without reading a symbol.

locations.note: RVA 0x23F7F7, storing the CGameLoader vtable at offset 2688 of a CScene.

records.title: 44 typed fields recovered, 29 of them confirmed twice over
records.summary: Everything a constructor writes into its object at a non-zero offset names what sits there. Where the vtable belongs to the constructor's own class the offset is a base subobject of its hierarchy, and the RTTI records that vtable's subobject offset independently: the two agree on 29 of the 44 entries, which is a second source saying the same thing rather than the same source said twice. Where the vtable belongs to a different class the offset names an embedded member and its type, and there are 15 of those. CScene is the clearest: a CLightMgr at 64, a CGameW at 88, a CChain at 112, a CEventMission at 592, a CGameLoader at 2688, a CList of CNonPlayer at 3312, a second CChain at 4256, a CLightStatic at 7552 and a CCameraMiniDemo at 22832. Layout only, from instruction encodings and the type information the compiler emitted; no field contents are read.

locations.note: CScene, constructed at RVA 0x23F7C4 onwards, with typed members at offsets 64 through 22832.

locations.symbol: base subobject offsets agreeing with the RTTI
locations.note: CEm021, CEm029Cart and CNonPlayer carry base subobjects at offsets 96, 208, 272, 384 and 592, each offset also recorded by the RTTI for that vtable.

records.title: Restated: the constructor-store counts, with a pointer to where they were raised
records.summary: The constructor stores were published at 270 stores of a taken address into the first argument, 265 of them landing on a known vtable, and 44 field-layout entries of which 29 are confirmed independently by the type information. Carrying `this` through an interior address added nine stores and three layout entries: 279, 274 and 47, with the independent confirmation unchanged at 29 and the ratio holding at 98.2 per cent against 98.1. That was stated in a separate packet about the receiver analysis and never linked back to here, which is the drift this record closes. The reading is untouched — an address written into an object at a fixed offset is overwhelmingly a vtable, and 146 functions still store one at offset zero.
